en.name: Stanislaus of Krakow
en.summary: Bishop of Krakow killed by King Boleslaus II after publicly rebuking him for injustice and immorality, becoming Poland's principal patron saint.
en.body: Stanislaus served as bishop of Krakow during the reign of the Polish king Boleslaus II, and became engaged in an escalating conflict with the king over what Stanislaus regarded as serious abuses of royal power and personal immorality, ultimately excommunicating the king in response to his conduct, a direct challenge to royal authority in an era when such confrontations were rare and dangerous. According to the tradition recorded shortly after the events, the enraged king had Stanislaus killed personally, some accounts hold by the king's own hand, while the bishop was celebrating Mass, a killing that scandalized the kingdom and contributed to Boleslaus's eventual overthrow and exile. The parallel to Thomas Becket's later murder in a similar church-state confrontation was frequently noted by medieval commentators. Stanislaus's cult grew rapidly in the following century, and he became the principal patron saint of Poland, seen as a symbol of moral courage against unjust royal power. He was canonized in 1253.
